Check interval coverage by simulation

Source: R/ctCoverageCheck.R
ctCoverageCheck.Rd

Performs a coverage check analysis by generating data from a model, fitting it multiple times with different fit arguments, and plotting the results. Works with fitArgs/ fittingModel combinations that fit with either backend='julia' (the ctFit default) or backend='stan'.

Usage

ctCoverageCheck(
  initialData,
  fittingModel,
  niter,
  fitArgs,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  fitCores = 1,
  generateCores = fitCores,
  plotEvery = max(c(10, cores))
)

Arguments

initialData

An initial dataset to fit to determine 'true' parameters for further generation.

fittingModel

A ctModel object used for fitting the data

niter

Number of iterations to run

fitArgs

Named list of fit argument sets to test (e.g., list(boot = list(optimcontrol = list(uncertainty = 'bootstrap')), hess = list(optimcontrol = list(uncertainty = 'hessian'))))

cores

The most CPU cores the check uses at once. Iterations run cores %/% fitCores at a time, each fit on fitCores.

fitCores

Number of cores for each inner ctFit call, at most cores. It replaces any cores given in fitArgs.

generateCores

Number of cores for ctGenerateFromFit when generating replicated datasets, at most cores. Defaults to fitCores; set it explicitly to use more cores for generation.

plotEvery

Print plots every n iterations; by default every 10, or every cores iterations when that is more.

Value

A list containing the results data.table and final plots

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Does the Hessian interval cover as often as it says? 100 datasets
# generated from the fit to ctstantestdat, each fitted twice.
model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
  LAMBDA = matrix(1))
check <- ctCoverageCheck(ctstantestdat, model, niter = 100,
  fitArgs = list(
    hessian = list(optimcontrol = list(uncertainty = 'hessian')),
    bootstrap = list(optimcontrol = list(uncertainty = 'bootstrap'))),
  cores = 4)
} # }
